Conditional Gaussian observed-item identification requires known finite positive calibration, distinct conditionally independent observations, identifiable joint probabilities, both zygosities, and stated moderator support. Continuous/disjoint-support argument requires common exact loglinear variance functions and at least four equality points per zygosity; four is sufficient, not necessary.

Non-Gaussian fixed-parameter latent-moment inverse is not an observed-response identification theorem. Population identification does not imply finite-MLE existence/uniqueness or MCMC convergence; all-zero response example shows nonexistence, not multiple maxima. Rasch raw-total sufficiency preserves latent-only target only for fixed known calibration and appropriate observed masks; it is distinct from standardized-total Gaussian comparator and supplies no measured speedup.
Completed centered12k four-chain gate is correctly recorded as joint failure; individual parameter performance does not certify joint convergence. Final recovery result is explicitly withheld.
